newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's 1996 GDP said to have grown 2.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's 1996 GDP said to have grown 2.1 pct.

text.p: Colombia's economy grew by an anemic 2.1 percent in 1996, well below the government's official target of growth up to 4.5 percent, Bogota's El Espectador newspaper reported Monday.
It said the growth figure, the lowest since 1991 and roughly in line with Colombia's population growth, was based on the most recent study by the National Planning Department.
Official gross domestic product figures for 1996 have not yet been made available, but the private National Financial Industries Association has estimated growth at 2.5 percent.

The political crisis stemming from charges that President Ernesto Samper financed his 1994 election campaign with drug money has been widely cited as one of the reasons for a sharp slowdown in economic growth last year.
Annual GDP growth averaged 4.5 percent over the past decade.
